admiral:noun.blurb: From Arabic amir, 'commander', by way of Old French.

alcohol:noun.blurb: From Arabic al-kuhl, itself from Aramaic.

algebra:noun.blurb: Coined in medieval Latin from Arabic al-jabr.

alpaca:noun.blurb: From Aymara allpaqa, by way of Spanish.

azure:noun.blurb: From Arabic lazaward, the stone the colour is named for.

ballet:noun.blurb: From French ballet, from Italian balletto, a diminutive of ballo 'dance'.

bamboo:noun.blurb: From Kannada, a Dravidian word for the plant.

banjo:noun.blurb: From Kimbundu mbanza, by way of the American South.

barbecue:noun.blurb: From Taíno barbacoa, a wooden framework, via Spanish.

boondocks.blurb: From Tagalog bundok 'mountain', via US troops in the Philippines.

caravan:noun.blurb: From Persian karvan, a company of desert travellers.

cheetah:noun.blurb: From Sanskrit chitraka, 'the spotted one', by way of Hindi.

cipher:noun.blurb: From Old French cifre, from Arabic sifr, 'zero'.

cockatoo:noun.blurb: From Malay kakaktua, by way of Dutch.

coffee.blurb: From Arabic qahwah, by way of Dutch koffie.

condor:noun.blurb: From Quechua kuntur, by way of Spanish.

cotton:noun.blurb: From Arabic qutn, via Old French coton.

coyote:noun.blurb: From Mexican Spanish, then Nahuatl coyotl.

dinghy:noun.blurb: From Bengali or Hindi dingi, a small boat.

elapse.blurb: From Middle French, from Latin elapsus, 'to slip away' (e- + labi).

gazelle:noun.blurb: From Arabic ghazal, by way of French.

geyser.blurb: From Icelandic Geysir, the famous hot spring, from geysa 'to gush'.

guard:noun.blurb: From Old French garde, of Germanic (Frankish) origin.

guru:noun.blurb: From Hindi guru 'teacher', from Sanskrit guru 'venerable, weighty'.

guy:noun.blurb: From Guy Fawkes, whose effigy was burned on 5 November.

harmattan:noun.blurb: From Akan, the dry wind off the Sahara.

iguana:noun.blurb: From Taíno iwana, by way of Spanish.

jar:noun.blurb: From Arabic jarra, a water pot.

jerky:noun.blurb: From Quechua ch'arki, by way of Spanish charqui.

juggernaut:noun.blurb: From Sanskrit Jagannatha, 'lord of the world', whose festival cart was said to crush devotees.

jungle.blurb: From Hindi jangal 'wilderness, forest', from Sanskrit jangala.

junk:noun.blurb: From Javanese djong, a sailing ship.

kangaroo:noun.blurb: From Guugu Yimidhirr gangurru, recorded by Cook's crew.

karaoke.blurb: Japanese kara 'empty' + oke (short for okestora) 'orchestra', an 'empty orchestra'.

ketchup:noun.blurb: From a Chinese dialect word for fish sauce, via Malay.

kiosk:noun.blurb: From Ottoman Turkish köşk, 'pavilion', which reached English through Italian and French.

kiwi:noun.blurb: From Maori kiwi, the bird, later the fruit.

koala:noun.blurb: From Dharug gula, recorded by settlers.

leg:noun.blurb: From Old Norse leggr, replacing Old English sceanc.

lemon:noun.blurb: Reached English through Old French and Arabic.

lime:noun.blurb: From Arabic lima, by way of French and Spanish.

magazine:noun.blurb: From Arabic makhzan 'storehouse', via Italian and Middle French.

malaria.blurb: Italian mala aria, 'bad air', from the old belief about swamp vapours.

mammoth.blurb: From Russian mammut, probably from a Siberian (Mansi) source word.

mango:noun.blurb: Reached English by way of Portuguese, from a Dravidian word for the fruit.

may:verb.blurb: Old English mæg "am able", from Proto-Germanic root *mag-

moa:noun.blurb: From Maori moa, an extinct bird.

paddy:noun.blurb: From Malay padi, rice in the husk.

paparazzi.blurb: Italian, from Fellini's La Dolce Vita (1960): the photographer Paparazzo.

papaya:noun.blurb: From Arawak, by way of Spanish.

phone:noun.blurb: Clipped from telephone: Greek tele 'far' + phone 'voice'.

pizza:noun.blurb: From Italian pizza, popularized in the US by returning WWII soldiers.

potato:noun.blurb: From Spanish patata, from Taíno batata.

proa:noun.blurb: From Malay prau, a sailing boat.

quinine:noun.blurb: From Quechua kina, the bark it comes from.

rickshaw.blurb: Japanese jinrikisha, 'man-powered vehicle', shortened in English.

robot:noun.blurb: Coined in Czech (robota, 'forced labor') by Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R.

safari.blurb: From Swahili safari 'journey', from Arabic safar 'to travel'.

samovar.blurb: Russian samovar, 'self-boiler', the tea urn of Russian tradition.

savanna:noun.blurb: From Taíno zabana, by way of Spanish sabana.

serendipity.blurb: Coined by Horace Walpole from the Persian tale of the Three Princes of Serendip (Sri Lanka).

soy:noun.blurb: From Japanese shoyu, from Chinese jiangyou.

taboo:noun.blurb: From Tongan tabu, recorded on Cook's voyages.

take:verb.blurb: From Old Norse taka, which displaced the native verb.

taro:noun.blurb: From Polynesian taro, recorded on Cook's voyages.

tattoo:noun.blurb: From Dutch tap-toe, 'shut the tap': the drumbeat that ordered soldiers back to their quarters.

tea:noun.blurb: Via Dutch thee from Min Nan Chinese te, the 'te' branch of the word's world map.

their:determiner.blurb: From Old Norse theirra, displacing Old English hira.

them:pronoun.blurb: From Old Norse theim, replacing Old English him.

they.blurb: Old Norse their, one of the pronouns borrowed wholesale from Norse.

thug:noun.blurb: From Hindi thag, a member of a robber band.

tiki:noun.blurb: From Maori tiki, an image of a god.

tycoon.blurb: Japanese taikun, 'great lord', the shogun's title, later applied to US magnates.

typhoon.blurb: From Cantonese taai fung 'great wind', blended with earlier trade-wind forms.

video:noun.blurb: From Latin videre 'to see', coined on the model of audio.

voodoo:noun.blurb: From Fon vodun, 'spirit', by way of the Caribbean.

window:noun.blurb: Old Norse vindauga, 'wind-eye', replacing Old English eagduru.

yam:noun.blurb: From West African nyami, by way of Portuguese inhame.

yogurt.blurb: From Turkish yogurt, perhaps related to yogun 'thick'.

zero:numeral.blurb: From Arabic sifr, 'nothing', by way of Italian.

zombie:noun.blurb: From Kongo nzambi, a spirit of the dead.
